intro: To fix a cursor that has disappeared or frozen in Pages on your Mac, first identify if the issue is with the mouse pointer or the blinking text insertion point. You can usually resolve these problems by switching document modes, force quitting the application, or adjusting your macOS accessibility settings.
tldr: Check if you are in Page Layout mode, which requires text boxes for typing.
Use Command + Option + Esc to force quit and relaunch Pages if the app is unresponsive.
Toggle your pointer size in System Settings if your mouse cursor is invisible.
Avoid accidental trackpad touches that move your cursor while you type.
Check for macOS updates to resolve system-wide input bugs.

blocks.text: Understanding the difference between mouse and text cursors

When you search for how to fix cursor on Mac, you might mean two different things. The first is the mouse pointer, the arrow you use to click menus and buttons. The second is the text insertion point, the thin vertical line that blinks where your text will appear. Most users who report a broken cursor in Pages are actually dealing with a locked insertion point.

If your mouse pointer vanishes, the issue is likely with macOS itself rather than the Pages application. If you cannot click into a document to start typing, the issue is almost certainly within the settings or the format of the document you have open. Distinguishing between these two will save you time.
Fixing the text insertion point in Pages

The most common reason for a missing text cursor in Pages is the document mode. Apple Pages offers two distinct document types: Word Processing and Page Layout. In a Word Processing document, you can click anywhere and start typing. In a Page Layout document, you must place text inside a text box. If you try to click on the background of a Page Layout document, nothing will happen.

To check your document mode, look at the File menu. If you see an option that says Convert to Word Processing, you are currently in Page Layout mode. Click that option to switch your document. Once switched, your insertion point should appear immediately when you click on the page canvas.
Troubleshooting a frozen or unresponsive Pages app

If the entire application stops responding and your cursor turns into the spinning beach ball, you need to force the app to close. Do not wait for it to recover if it has been stuck for more than a minute. Press ⌘ Command + ⌥ Option + Esc on your keyboard to open the Force Quit menu. Select Pages from the list and press Return to end the process.

After you force quit, wait a few seconds before opening Pages again. If the problem persists, try restarting your Mac. A full system restart clears the temporary cache files that sometimes interfere with input detection. Ensure you save any other open work before you perform this step.
Adjusting system settings for cursor visibility

If your mouse pointer is invisible, your system settings might be the culprit. Navigate to the Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility > Display. Look for the Pointer size slider. If it is set to the smallest increment, try increasing it slightly. Sometimes, this action forces the system to redraw the pointer on the screen.

Also check if you have any third-party mouse software installed. Apps that customize mouse behavior can sometimes conflict with macOS updates. If you recently updated your Mac to a new version of macOS, check the developer website for those mouse apps to see if a compatibility patch is available.
Preventing accidental cursor jumps while typing

Many users complain that their cursor jumps to a different line while they are typing. This is often caused by the trackpad on your MacBook. If your palms or thumbs brush against the trackpad surface, the cursor will move to that location. To fix this, you can adjust your trackpad sensitivity in System Settings.

Go to System Settings > Trackpad. You can reduce the tracking speed or turn off features like Tap to click if you find you are triggering them by mistake. Another fix is to use an external keyboard and mouse and disable the trackpad entirely when you are doing heavy writing work. This ensures your hands stay clear of the input surface.
What to do if the problem is system-wide

If you find that your cursor is missing in all applications, not just Pages, the issue is deeper than your document settings. Check if your mouse or trackpad has enough battery. If you use a wireless mouse, replace the batteries or charge it. A low-power connection can cause the cursor to stutter or disappear.

You should also check for pending macOS updates. Apple frequently releases patches that fix bugs related to input hardware and UI rendering. Go to System Settings > General > Software Update to see if your Mac is running the latest version. Keeping your system current is the best way to prevent these types of glitches from recurring.

faq.question: Why can I not click to type in my Pages document?
faq.answer: You are likely in Page Layout mode. Go to the File menu and select Convert to Word Processing to enable standard text entry.

faq.question: How do I fix a frozen cursor in Pages?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ Command + ⌥ Option + Esc to open the Force Quit menu, select Pages, and choose Force Quit.

faq.question: Is there a specific setting for the text cursor?
faq.answer: There is no direct setting for the text cursor in Pages, but you can change your system-wide pointer size in System Settings > Accessibility > Display.

steps.name: Check Document Mode
steps.text: If you cannot click to type, verify your document format. Click the File menu and look for Convert to Word Processing. If you see this, your document is in Page Layout mode, which does not allow for free-flowing text entry.

steps.name: Force Quit Pages
steps.text: If the app is frozen, press the force quit shortcut to close it immediately. This clears the unresponsive state.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer Size
steps.text: If your mouse pointer is invisible, go to System Settings and increase the size of the pointer to make it visible again.
